correctness.rationale: A rigorous pentagon frustration lower bound and hexagon facial-parity bijection to the 125 perfect matchings of the icosahedron and 64 face choices establish exhaustiveness of 16,000 ground states. Paired pentagon spin sums cancel, giving zero magnetization for each state. The exact 8,000-state signed Gram matrix B=X^TX/32 has integer entries and, as directly reproduced by the packaged checker, satisfies (B-50I)(B-74I)(B-104I)(B-560I)(B^2-1308B+68596I)=0. Exact integer/rational Gaussian elimination yields factor kernel dimensions 11,5,4,4,6 and hence exactly the seven advertised C eigenvalues with multiplicities; 30 zeros come from the opposite-spin cross-pentagon constraints. All 1,770 pair correlations and trace are checked. Numerical runs do not substitute for the analytical exhaustive-coverage argument.

value.rationale: The local-field zero-temperature susceptibility spectrum is a natural complete response invariant for a physically canonical frustrated C60 lattice, not an arbitrary parameter slice. It resolves a substantial 30-dimensional silent-versus-responsive field subspace, an algebraic square-root-of-five spectral splitting, and vanishing uniform-field Curie response despite 16,000 ground states. This yields precise stringent benchmarks for simulations and separates classical Ising response from SU(2) quantum-correlation studies. The old count alone does not imply the spectrum; no unproved downstream material behavior is claimed.
